newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Legal challenges by Indonesian leader mired again.
newsitem.headline: Legal challenges by Indonesian leader mired again.

text.p: Legal challenges by Indonesia's Megawati Sukarnoputri against her removal as head of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) were mired again on Wednesday as her latest lawsuit was adjourned without a hearing.

Judge Soehardjo adjourned a case filed by Megawati against the General Election Institute (LPU) and its chairman, Interior Minister Yogie Memet, for rejecting her list of candidates for next year's general elections because the government was not represented.
"We must wait two weeks as they have not yet chosen any lawyers," Megawati's chief lawyer R.O. Tambunan said.
Megawati has said that as the legal head of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), the LPU must accept her list of candidates for the elections due in May next year.
The LPU instead accepted a list submitted by a faction of the PDI, which the government has said is the genuine representative of the party.
Indonesia allows only three recognised politial parties to contest elections -- the ruling Golkar, the PDI and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party.
It was one of a series of cases filed by Megawati, daughter of late founding president Sukarno, against the government over her removal from the PDI leadership in June.
Political analysts have said the government moved to sideline Megawati because it feared she could draw votes from Golkar during the elections.

She has appealed to the Jakarta High Court against a lower court's refusal to hear a lawsuit against the military and the government for backing the rival PDI faction. The lower court said it did not have the jurisdiction to hear the case.
She has also filed suit against the mayor of East Jakarta for closing down her temporary headquarters on the grounds that it violated zoning regulations. That case is to be taken up next week.
Also on Wednesday, a detective was warned against perjury in a trial of 11 of 124 supporters of Megawati who have been charged with assault and disobeying police.
They were arrested after police and members of the rival PDI faction raided the party headquarters on July 27, which Megawati's supporters had taken over in protest against her ouster.
The raid triggered the worst riots in Jakarta for over 20 years. At least five people died.

Judge Gatam Taridi warned Captain Edward Syah Pernong, head of the Central Jakarta police detective section, after he repeatedly answered "I don't know" and "I cannot recall" to questions during cross-examination.

Pernong testifed that he had gone to PDI headquarters early on the morning of July 27 with the intention of making arrests but he said he could not recall and would not estimate how many people were attacking the office or what they were wearing.
Defence lawyers have complained only Megawati loyalists inside the building were arrested and charged.
During the cross-examination by Tambunan, Pernong eventually admitted supporters of the rival faction attacked the PDI office.
"We did not arrest any of those outside because they were part of a crowd," Pernong explained.
The prosecution has said those arrested threw stones at people outside the building, injuring several, and refused to disperse when ordered to do so.
